redFlags.link: When should I see a doctor?
redFlags.title: When to see a doctor
redFlags.intro: Hot flushes and night sweats are common in menopause. Some symptoms are not typical and should be checked:
redFlags.urgentTitle: Same day – or call emergency services
urgent: Very heavy bleeding – soaking a pad or tampon every hour for several hours.
Chest pain, sudden shortness of breath, or a painful, swollen leg.
A sudden severe headache, weakness on one side or trouble speaking.
soon: Any bleeding after 12 months without a period.
Bleeding between periods or after sex.
Periods that are much heavier or longer than usual.
Night sweats with fever or weight loss you can't explain.
Low mood on most days for more than two weeks.
redFlags.routine: If nothing above applies, bring your log to your next appointment – months of notes make the conversation easier.
redFlags.disclaimer: General information, not a diagnosis. If in doubt, call your doctor.
